features.title: Fall back to the main gateway URL when a stale resume_gateway_url is unreachable
features.user_visible_behavior: A shard whose persisted resume_gateway_url points at a Discord edge that no longer serves it (503 on the WebSocket handshake, before IDENTIFY) discards the resume tuple after 3 consecutive dial-stage failures in which that host answered and refused the upgrade, then reconnects via wss://gateway.discord.gg/, instead of redialing the dead host once per second forever. The cleared tuple is persisted, so a pod restart cannot reload the dead host. The reconnect loop backs off exponentially (1s -> 60s, jittered) instead of retrying flat 1s. A resume host that never answers at all (decommissioned edge, DNS/TLS/refused) is escaped once it has been unreachable for MaxResumeNoResponseDuration (1h) without a single successful dial, so it cannot trap the shard forever either. Both discards now log loudly enough to alert on: never-answered at ERROR, answered-and-refused at WARN.

features.notes: TATSU-2514 (prod incident 2026-09-01: 41/1024 shards stuck, zero self-healing, pods stayed 1/1 Running). Only DIAL-stage failures against the resume URL are counted - failures against the main gateway URL have no resume state to blame, and a cancelled connection context (shutdown / Cancel / ForceIdentify) is our own teardown and is not counted. The invalidation reuses the exact mechanism ForceIdentify already proved in production; this PR only gives it an automatic trigger. Recovery costs a full re-IDENTIFY and shard re-backfill (~1,400 guilds), which is why the threshold is 3 and not 1. NOT DONE in this PR (ticket bullet 4, explicitly 'Consider'): a metric/alert on 'shard has not reached ready in N minutes' - this outage class is still invisible to monitoring. Backoff must stay interruptible: Open clears Session.cur on return, so Session.Cancel cannot reach a shard that is between attempts — the Manager's per-shard wake channel is what keeps RestartShard/gwForceIdentify prompt. Both staging follow-ups are FIXED in 8374671 and re-validated: the failure ladder now resets when the tuple is discarded (the next dial targets a different host, so the accumulated delay predicts nothing), cutting escape from 15.8s to 8.1s; and the duplicate 'shard' log field is gone, pinned by a test. PR #87 review (weiyuan-tatsu, CHANGES_REQUESTED) raised 2 findings, both fixed. F1 (P1): only a dial failure the host ANSWERED (non-nil *http.Response, i.e. it refused the upgrade) may consume a strike -- verified against nhooyr.io/websocket@v1.8.6 that every no-response transport failure (DNS/TLS/refused/egress) yields a nil response, so counting them would let one shared outage clear valid resume tuples fleet-wide and force a re-IDENTIFY + re-backfill per shard. noteDialFailure now takes (usedResumeURL, hostResponded); an unanswered dial is ignored, NOT forgiving, so it cannot reset strikes earned mid-run of 503s. F2 (P2): the backoff ladder scored health on total Open duration, which wraps acquireIdentifyLock's 160s timeout -- an attempt could wait out the lock, fail its first dial, and still reset the ladder to base every time, defeating the backoff in exactly the fleet-wide identify contention it damps. Open now returns connected time measured from the existing markReady (READY/RESUMED) milestone via conn.readyFor; the close line logs connected_for and attempt_took. Prior staging evidence still valid (checked, not assumed): the repro's wss://example.com answers HTTP 200 so resp is non-nil and still counts, and attempts 1-3 never reach READY so the ladder input is 0 under both wirings. OPEN QUESTION back to the reviewer: F1's narrowing reopens the trap for an edge that is decommissioned rather than 503-ing (hostname stops resolving => nil response forever => no strike => only gwForceIdentify recovers it); a second, much higher no-response threshold would close it, but that is the broader policy the reviewer explicitly deferred, so it is their call. DECOMMISSIONED-EDGE GAP CLOSED on maintainer's call: F1 was a regression, not just an uncovered case (master escaped a non-resolving edge after 3 strikes; post-F1 it never would). Added MaxResumeNoResponseFailures=60 as an independent budget for unanswered dials, so fleet-safety and eventual escape both hold. Sized for safety not speed: 60 strikes = ~55min (~62 with jitter), past the point a Discord RESUME would be honoured, so it pre-empts an INVALID_SESSION-driven re-IDENTIFY rather than causing one; ~20 strikes (~16min) was drafted and rejected as landing inside the window where a RESUME might still work. Cascade risk checked in code: initEtcd buckets the identify mutex by shardID%16 so a fleet-wide re-IDENTIFY drains serially through 16 buckets (~11min at calcIdentifyWait=10s, ~75min with member processing) and cannot burst at Discord; the real cost is that a shard holding a resume tuple SKIPS the identify lock, so mass invalidation converts fast ungated recovery into that gated drain -- hence the high threshold. Budgets are independent, neither clears the other, both reset on a successful dial; distinct log message and discardResumeState helper shared by both triggers. POST-STAGING FOLLOW-UP (2 maintainer challenges, both landed): (1) MaxResumeNoResponseFailures=60 replaced by MaxResumeNoResponseDuration=1h with Session.resumeNoResponseSince - a strike count only approximated elapsed time via the reconnect ladder, so retuning the ladder would silently redefine the threshold while its justification read the same; elapsed time is what makes discarding safe, so the code now says so. Only a successful dial clears the window. noteDialFailureAt injects the clock. The 'a Discord session will not survive an hour' premise is REASONED not measured; acceptable only because the error is one-sided (too long delays an escape that previously never happened; too short mass-invalidates during a shared outage). (2) Discard log levels raised because they are currently the ONLY alerting: never-answered -> ERROR (shard down ~1h with nothing answering = incident), answered-and-refused -> WARN (routine edge retirement must not cry wolf). Pinned behaviourally via a slog.Sink capture test asserting e.Level, not by source text. slogtest fatals on Error lines, hence IgnoreErrors in the window test. CAVEAT: the discard line only fires for shards that HAVE a resume tuple - a shard failing forever against the main gateway URL emits none, so this is a partial net, not a substitute for TATSU-2516.
